extracted.intended_audience: small business concerns (SBCs), grant administrators, and prospective NIH SBIR/STTR applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Policy and compliance requirements for applying to and receiving NIH SBIR and STTR awards, including eligibility, effort rules, IP/data rights, cost/indirect cost guidance, certifications, and reporting obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted program transitions / switching
rubrics_metrics.description: SBIR/STTR program policy allows Phase I and Phase II recipients to apply across SBIR and STTR phases and to switch programs to any active and open NIH SBIR or STTR solicitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific allowed transitions are enumerated (e.g., Phase I STTR → NIH SBIR/STTR Phase II; Phase II SBIR → Phase IIB or CRP; Phase IIB → CRP). Applicants that 'switch' must comply with the policies for the program and NOFO to which they submit the application. See SBIR/STTR Life Cycle Certification sections for further information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fast-Track application process
rubrics_metrics.description: Fast-Track allows Phase I and Phase II grant applications to be submitted and reviewed together and receive a single rating to expedite award decisions for meritorious projects with high commercialization potential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are strongly encouraged to consult with cognizant NIH program staff before submitting to assure Fast-Track is appropriate. See SF424 (R&R) SBIR/STTR Application Guide for submission details.

rubrics_metrics.name: General eligibility — United States small business concern (SBC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only United States small business concerns (SBCs) are eligible to submit SBIR and STTR applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If eligibility is unclear, NIH will request a size determination by the SBA and will not make an SBIR or STTR award until the SBA provides a determination. Contact the SBA Size District Office for further information.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR: Organized for profit and U.S. place of business
rubrics_metrics.description: The SBIR applicant must be organized for profit with a place of business located in the United States and operate primarily within the United States or make a significant contribution to the U.S. economy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes payment of taxes or use of American products/materials as evidence of significant contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR: Permitted legal forms
rubrics_metrics.description: The SBIR applicant may be an individual proprietorship, partnership, LLC, corporation, joint venture, association, trust or cooperative, with joint ventures limited by foreign participation rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the form is a joint venture, there must be less than 50 percent participation by foreign business entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR: Ownership and control tests
rubrics_metrics.description: An SBIR concern must be more than 50% directly owned and controlled by qualifying U.S. individuals/entities OR be more than 50% owned by multiple venture capital operating companies/hedge funds/private equity firms (no single such firm >50%), OR be a joint venture meeting the specified ownership tests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed subparagraphs (c.i–c.iii) describe the acceptable ownership structures; joint ventures including entities meeting paragraph (ii) must comply with registration/application rules (§121.705(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Size limit (employees) and affiliation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The concern, including its affiliates, must have not more than 500 employees and meet other regulatory requirements in 13 CFR Part 121.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affiliation is determined when one concern controls or has the power to control another, or a third party controls both; control can be exercised via ownership, management, or contractual relationships. 'Affiliates' and 'number of employees' are defined in 13 CFR Part 121.

rubrics_metrics.name: STTR: Organized for profit and U.S. place of business
rubrics_metrics.description: STTR applicants must be organized for profit with a U.S. place of business and operate primarily in the United States or make a significant contribution to the U.S. economy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mirrors SBIR requirement (legal form, U.S. operations) but STTR ownership/control subparagraphs differ (see STTR-specific clauses).

rubrics_metrics.name: STTR: Ownership and joint venture rules
rubrics_metrics.description: STTR concerns must be more than 50% directly owned and controlled by U.S. individuals/entities OR be a joint venture in which each entity meets the >50% direct ownership/control requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: STTR does not include the alternative ownership-by-private-equity/VC pathway that SBIR allows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place of performance
rubrics_metrics.description: For both Phase I and Phase II awards, the research or R&D project activity must be performed in its entirety in the United States (50 states, territories, Puerto Rico, certain freely associated states, and D.C.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH no longer recognizes foreign subawards; collaborative international research must use the collaborative international research award mechanism (see Section 16.8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Change in organization size and required advance notice for legal actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant organization eligibility is determined at the time of the initial award; recipients must give NIH advance notice for legal actions (merger, acquisition, successor-in-interest) as soon as possible but no later than 30 days before the proposed change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a transferee cannot recertify small business status, NIH will not issue continued awards to the transferee and will terminate existing awards to the original recipient. Recipients should contact the NIH awarding office when considering a move to a new organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum level of effort — SBIR Phase I
rubrics_metrics.description: Under SBIR Phase I awards, a minimum of two-thirds (67%) of the research or analytical effort must be carried out by the SBC; payments to consultants/consortium participants/contractors generally may not exceed 33% of the total requested amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deviations may be considered on a case-by-case basis for SBIR only and must be approved in writing by the awarding IC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum level of effort — SBIR Phase II
rubrics_metrics.description: Under SBIR Phase II awards, a minimum of one-half (50%) of the research or analytical effort must be carried out by the SBC; payments to consultants/consortium participants/contractors generally may not exceed 50% of the total requested amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deviations may be considered on a case-by-case basis for SBIR only and must be approved in writing by the awarding IC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum level of effort — STTR (Phase I & II)
rubrics_metrics.description: For STTR awards, at least 40% of the work must be performed by the SBC and at least 30% by the single, non-profit research institution; these percentages are Congressionally mandated and waivers are not permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Percentages are determined based on total cost (direct + indirect costs, and fee) attributable to each party, unless otherwise justified in the 'Consortium/Contractual Arrangements' portion of the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRP subcontracting and SBC substantive role
rubrics_metrics.description: For CRP awards, an SBC may subcontract a substantial portion to third parties, but the SBC must perform a substantive role in planned research and not merely serve as a conduit of funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At minimum, this includes providing appropriate oversight of all scientific, programmatic, financial, and administrative matters related to the grant; extent depends on nature of outsourced effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple PD/PI rules and employment/effort requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The SBC is always the applicant/awardee; organizations other than the SBC with PD/PIs are subcontractors. For SBIR Phase I, the Contact PD/PI must meet the primary employment requirement (more than half of time employed by SBC) though deviations may be approved in exceptional circumstances. For Phase II and CRP, the Contact PD/PI must meet primary employment; for STTR PD/PIs are not required to be SBC employees but the Contact PD/PI must have a formal appointment/commitment to the SBC. Each PD/PI on a multiple PD/PI award must commit a minimum of 1.2 calendar months (10% effort).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To receive a deviation for Phase I primary employment, a small business must show significant PI employment at the company, significant commitment to the project, and commitment to transition the PI to 51%+ employment in Phase II. STTR applicants must officially affiliate a PD/PI with the SBC in eRA Commons if the PD/PI is not an employee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public policy: financial conflicts of interest and procurement preference
rubrics_metrics.description: For-profit organizations receiving SBIR/STTR awards are generally subject to the same public policy requirements as non-profits, but FCOI reporting requirements do not apply to Phase I SBIR/STTR; they do apply to Phase II, Phase IIB and CRP. When purchasing equipment/products under the award, SBCs should purchase American-made items whenever possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Public Policy Requirements and Financial Conflict of Interest sections for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required disclosures of foreign affiliations / due diligence
rubrics_metrics.description: As required by the SBIR/STTR Extension Act of 2022, NIH assesses security risks and requires disclosure of all funded and unfunded relationships with foreign countries for all owners and covered individuals; applicants must submit the Required Disclosures form via Just-In-Time (JIT).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH may request additional documentation (contracts, financial obligations) covering the prior 5-year period. NIH may decline to award based on identified risks; active awardees may be required to disclose and can be terminated for prohibited risks. See Foreign Disclosure and Risk Management webpage for details and case studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program levels (total costs) and budget requests
rubrics_metrics.description: SBA provides program levels for SBIR and STTR based on statutory guidelines; agencies may issue awards up to the SBA guideline when the proposed budget and period are fully justified. Applicants must request an appropriate level in the competing application; applications will not be adjusted after submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SBA may adjust award guidelines annually; NIH has received waivers to exceed SBA levels under certain circumstances—see NIH's SBIR web page for current waiver topics and budget levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Profit or fee rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A reasonable profit or fee may be paid to an SBC under Phase I, Phase II or CRP but must be included in the budget request at time of application. The profit/fee is not considered a 'cost' for certain determinations and normally will not exceed 7% of total costs for each phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Profit/fee should be drawn from PMS proportionally to drawdown of direct and indirect costs. Profit applies solely to the SBC receiving the award, though the SBC may pay profit/fee to a contractor for routine goods or services per normal commercial practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect cost rate guidance — Phase I
rubrics_metrics.description: If the SBC has a currently effective indirect cost rate with a Federal agency, use that rate (adjusted for IR&D). If not, propose estimated indirect costs at a rate not to exceed 40% of total direct costs. Only actual indirect costs may be charged to projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH will not negotiate indirect cost rates for Phase I awards. If awarded at ≤40%, the rate used to charge actual indirect costs cannot exceed the awarded rate unless the SBC negotiates with a Federal agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect cost rate guidance — Phase II and CRP
rubrics_metrics.description: If the SBC has a currently effective negotiated indirect cost rate, use it (adjusted for IR&D). If not, propose an estimated rate. If requested rate is ≤40% of total direct costs, no further justification is required; if >40%, DFAS will negotiate rates for Phase II or CRP awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon request, provide DFAS with an indirect cost proposal and supporting financial data for the most recently completed fiscal year, or estimated rates with support if data unavailable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative requirements and prohibition on market research funding
rubrics_metrics.description: For-profit SBIR/STTR recipients are subject to the same administrative requirements as non-profits (see 2 CFR Part 200). NIH will not support market research under the grant except for TABA funds or with the Commercialization Readiness Pilot (CRP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition of 'market research' provided; market research does not include surveys that are part of the research plan's objectives to determine impact on behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual property: general data and copyright rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Rights to data (including software) developed under NIH awards remain with the recipient, but copyrighted material is subject to a royalty-free, nonexclusive, irrevocable license to the Federal Government to reproduce, publish or otherwise use the material for Federal purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under SBIR/STTR programs, such data generally will not be released outside the Federal government without the recipient's permission for 20 years from completion of the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR/STTR data rights — statutory retention and government rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 9 of the Small Business Act provides for retention by an SBC of rights to data generated in performance of an SBIR/STTR award for a period of not less than 4 years; SBIR/STTR data rights grant the Government rights during the SBIR/STTR protection period but are intended to limit uses that would undermine SBC commercialization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Main elements: (a) SBC retains title/ownership of SBIR/STTR data it develops; (b) Government receives SBIR/STTR data rights during the protection period on appropriately marked data, with unlimited rights in Form, Fit, and Function Data, OMIT Data, and unmarked data; (c) after protection period expires, Government may use and authorize others to use the data for government purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR/STTR protection period length
rubrics_metrics.description: The SBIR/STTR protection period begins with the award and ends twenty years (or longer at agency discretion) from the date of award unless the agency and SBC negotiate another protection period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protection period applies to Phase I, II, and Federally-funded Phase III SBIR/STTR awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking and correction of SBIR/STTR data legends
rubrics_metrics.description: To receive SBIR/STTR protections, delivered SBIR/STTR data must be marked with the appropriate SBIR/STTR data rights legend/notice in accordance with agency procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If delivered without the required legend, the recipient may, within 6 months (or longer for good cause), request placement of an omitted legend. If delivered with an incorrect or nonconforming legend, the agency may correct or permit correction at the recipient's expense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negotiated rights and prohibition on conditioning awards
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency must not condition issuance of an SBIR/STTR award on the recipient negotiating or consenting to negotiate a specially negotiated license or other agreement regarding SBIR/STTR data; negotiation of such agreements is permitted only after award and must be voluntary and mutual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any bilateral data rights modification must be in writing, entered after the funding agreement is signed, and not a precondition for additional work or exercise of options. Any provision in a solicitation that would diminish SBIR/STTR data rights has no effect on resulting awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: STTR required IP allocation agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: The STTR program requires the small business recipient and the single, non-profit research institution to execute an agreement allocating intellectual property rights and rights, if any, to carry out follow-on research, development, or commercialization of the subject research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By signing the face page of the grant application, the SBC's AOR certifies the agreement is satisfactory and will be effective at time of award; a copy must be furnished to the NIH awarding IC prior to award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data sharing and 20-year non-release rule
rubrics_metrics.description: SBIR and STTR applicants must comply with NIH DMS policy as modified by the Small Business Act. Whether or not the award meets the threshold for data sharing, NIH will not release data outside the Federal government without the recipient's permission for 20 years from completion of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If final data are proprietary and not amenable to sharing, the SBC should explain that in the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR Life Cycle Certification requirements and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: All SBIR Phase I and Phase II recipients must complete a Life Cycle Certification at all times set forth in the Notice of Award (includes checking all boxes and authorized officer signature/date each time required).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A certification is required at specific times (e.g., Phase I: at time of receiving final payment/disbursement; Phase II: prior to receiving >50% of total award and prior to final payment). Certifications are submitted in I-RPPR and F-RPPR under Section G.1 and must be submitted via eRA Commons no later than 120 calendar days from the period of performance end date. I-RPPR/F-RPPR will not be accepted unless all completed certifications are received; failure may result in corrective actions, withholding of awards, suspension or termination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Life Cycle Certification attestation items — PI employment
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must verify and certify specific provisions; for example, that the principal investigator spent more than half of their time as an employee of the recipient or has requested and received a written deviation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a deviation is approved by NIH, the certification will document the adjusted percentage of time approved. Drawing/requesting funds from the Payment Management System indicates compliance with certification requirements; inability to complete certification should be reported to the GMO immediately.
